subject: When does it aid performance to put computations in the transformed parameters section?

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: When does it aid performance to put computations in the transformed parameters section?
parts:
Sometimes models have intermediary/derived quantities that could be computed in either be the model section or the transformed parameters section. An example would be the non-centered parameterization of a hierarchical regression (aka Matt trick). I thought I'd read in the manual that the declarations & computations in the transformed parameters section were computed less frequently than those in the model section, but now I see that Figure 29.1 (pg. 318 of manual v2.11.0) lists them both as being computed on each leapfrog step. On the other hand, if only the model block is used, one can put all the intermediary/derived quantities in a local block and avoid memory overhead of storing them across steps, right? So, are there cases that achieve performance speed ups by using the transformed parameters section?

Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] When does it aid performance to put computations in the transformed parameters section?
parts:
No, the only difference is that the transformed parameters
are saved and local variables in the model block are not.
Otherwise, they execute exactly the same code in C++.

We've been considering two competing changes:

* removing the transformed parameters block altogether (deprecating,
but still supporting for backward compatibility), and

* allowing increments to the log density in the transformed parameter
block that go into the Jacobian (and hence will be ignored for
maximum likelihood estimates)

- Bob
